findings.title: Generated cleanup command can recursively delete an unbounded path
findings.what: directRemovalSnippet accepts any non-empty removalPath and emits `rm -rf -- <quoted path>` for skills and plugins. Quoting prevents shell injection, but a malformed or poisoned configuration can supply `/`, a home directory, or another broad path; copying the generated remediation would recursively delete it.
findings.fix: Before emitting recursive removal, normalize and validate removalPath against the expected resource-specific Claude configuration/install roots and reject filesystem roots, home/config roots, traversal, and paths outside those roots; fall back to a non-executable manual instruction when validation fails.
findings.acceptance: Unit tests demonstrate that `/`, the user home, the Claude config root, traversal paths, and out-of-root plugin paths never produce `rm -rf`, while a valid nested skill or plugin installation path still produces a quoted command with `--`.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 13-16 have only a non-empty check before recursive deletion. The related baseline producer passes plugin installPath through as removalPath without a containment guarantee; shellQuote blocks injection but does not limit deletion scope.
